Trail running shoes buying guide

Before you buy trail running shoes, think about terrain, lug depth and fit. Heel-to-toe drop matters too.

1. Grip and lug depth

Lug depth of 4-6 mm works for mixed terrain. Vibram rubber lasts longer.

Fit and toe box

A wide toe box lets toes splay on descents.

How long do trail running shoes last?

Expect 300 to 500 miles.

Cushioning

Cushioning and stack height trade ground feel for comfort.
